source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use frequent personal self-disclosure to create a friendship and make the relationship less professionally bounded.","B":"Remain emotionally detached and avoid reflecting on personal reactions so the nurse's self never enters the interaction.","C":"Use self-awareness, presence, empathy, therapeutic communication, and professional boundaries to support the client's goals.","D":"Agree with the client's beliefs and decisions even when they conflict with therapeutic goals or professional judgment."}}
source_row.rationale: Therapeutic use of self involves intentional, self-aware use of presence, empathy, communication, and professional boundaries to support the client's therapeutic goals. Option C is correct. Extensive self-disclosure, emotional detachment, and indiscriminate agreement undermine the therapeutic relationship.
source_row.source_detail: Psychosocial Integrity activity statements/content examples: establish therapeutic relationships using therapeutic communication, support client coping and psychosocial needs, and maintain professional boundaries while providing client-centered care. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness live-rechecked 2026-08-15. source_row.stem: Which nursing action best demonstrates therapeutic use of self in a mental health setting?
